speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and when did you first notice it?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count. Can you tell me if you have been around anyone with a rash recently, and has the facial rash spread to your trunk?

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any small, raised, erythematous macules on your cheeks that look like a "slapped cheek" appearance? Also, does the rash on your trunk and extremities have a lacy or reticular pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities, is classic for Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
